name: Julius
title: The Kindly Centurion
summary: Julius was a centurion (officer) in the imperial cohort (the Augustan Cohort) who was given charge of escorting the apostle Paul and other prisoners from Caesarea to Rome. He showed kindness and respect to Paul during the dangerous sea voyage, and played a key role in saving Paul's life when the soldiers intended to kill the prisoners during the shipwreck off Malta.

keyEvents.title: Receives Responsibility for the Prisoners
keyEvents.description: Julius, a centurion in the Augustan Cohort, was tasked with escorting Paul and other prisoners from Caesarea to Rome to stand trial before the emperor.

keyEvents.title: Shows Kindness Toward Paul
keyEvents.description: During a stop at Sidon, Julius allowed Paul to go ashore to visit friends and be cared for, demonstrating his goodwill toward the apostle.

keyEvents.title: Disregards Paul's Warning
keyEvents.description: When Paul warned against continuing the journey from Fair Havens in Crete, Julius chose to listen to the ship's captain and owner instead of Paul, which led to a catastrophic storm.

keyEvents.title: Preventing the Killing of Prisoners During the Shipwreck
keyEvents.description: When the soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent escape during the shipwreck, Julius intervened and stopped them because he wanted to save Paul's life.

keyEvents.title: All Saved on Shore at Malta
keyEvents.description: Under Julius' leadership, everyone followed his orders to swim or hold onto planks, and all 276 people on board reached the island of Malta safely.
